match.reason: Neither bank point teaches recycling metals or the circular economy, saving ore and energy; the activity series and metallic bonding cover different ideas.

draft.title: Metal recycling
card: Metal recycling collects used metal, melts it and makes it into new products. This avoids mining and processing new ore, which is rock that contains a metal.
A circular economy keeps materials in use by reusing and recycling them. A linear economy takes resources, makes a product and throws it away.
Recycling saves ore, so fewer new mines are needed. It also usually saves energy, because melting scrap metal often needs less energy than extracting metal from ore.
Metals suit recycling because they can be melted and reshaped many times. Scrap metal must still be collected and sorted by type before it is melted.
draft.remember: Recycling metal keeps it in use, so less ore is mined and usually less energy is needed.

a.q: Which action is an example of a circular economy for metals?
opts: Melting old steel cans to make new steel products
Burying old steel cans in a landfill site
Mining more iron ore to make new steel cans
Storing old steel cans in a shed for many years
a.why: Melting old cans to make new products keeps the metal in use. Burying them is the linear path, where the metal is used once and thrown away.
a.clue: Which action puts the used metal back into use?

b.q: A Geelong company melts scrap aluminium to make new bike frames instead of using aluminium from new ore. What is a benefit of this choice?
opts: It saves ore and usually saves energy
It removes the need to collect scrap metal
It makes the metal lose its ability to be reshaped
It means the metal can only be used one more time
b.why: Scrap metal replaces ore, so less ore is needed, and melting scrap usually takes less energy than extracting metal from ore. The scrap still has to be collected and sorted, so that option is wrong.
b.clue: Think about what the scrap replaces.

a.best: Melting old steel cans to make new steel products

b.best: It saves ore and usually saves energy

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a qualifier ('usually') and the only one that names a benefit. The distractors are plainly drawbacks or false claims, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
